findings.summary: Task 4c.3 adds the ConversationStore implementation, the conversation revision check and the FB-2 fix to kernel/memory_store.py, which already has 499 lines. test_kernel_module_size applies MAX_KERNEL_MODULE_LINES = 500 to every kernel/*.py, so 4c.3 as written fails its own full gate. Global Constraints line 84 plans new modules only for routing and carrying. Fix: name a new kernel module, or a split of memory_store.py, in 4c.3's Files (ENG-WORK-1).

In conversations: shadow, messages go through the new route and the new store checks. A linked start calls create_run_idempotent with conversation_revision, which raises ConcurrencyConflict on a stale revision or on a concurrent second run. So shadow can refuse a message today's path accepts, against Review Focus 7 ('refuse no message') and D8's claim that the one-active-run check 'never fires' (it can, under a race). There is no fallback to POST /v1/runs when the conversation route fails in shadow; the UI fallback only changes the view. Shadow must act on the existing path (PR-22, PR-23, ENG-TOGGLE-1, ENG-TOGGLE-2). Fix: in shadow, skip the revision and active-run refusals, or record them as compared without refusing; and fall back to today's run and input routes when a conversation route errors. Add tests for a stale revision and a concurrent pair in shadow.

The answer route loses the pending-question binding. The message body's expected_revision is the conversation's revision, and only run creation bumps it. 4d.1 calls accept_input with the run's current revision as the router reads it. A message written against question Q1 therefore answers Q2 if the same run asked again in between. Today's /inputs route binds to the run revision the client saw. Retrying an answer is also unspecified: the input replay check lives in the HTTP handler (api.py), not in accept_input. After the answer moves the run to RUNNING, a retry is routed refuse and gets CONFLICT instead of the original result. Only test_retried_message_starts_one_run, which covers start, is named. Fix: bind answers to the run revision (or bump the conversation revision on every input request), make post_message idempotent for answers, and add test_retried_answer_is_accepted_once (PR-15, PR-17, ENG-TRUST-4).

Concern (a) is real. The answer verifiers build OutcomeReport without verified_values (answers.py _report), only the procurement write verifier sets it, and ir_on._kept drops it unless execution_ir is on. So run 2's findings can come only from D5's other clause, the arguments of a VERIFIED typed answer. ShortageAnswer (refs plus decimals, no free text) is a good carrier. But carry(runs, events_by_run, outcomes, classes) takes no action records, nothing checks that the shortage answer contract declares data_classes (unmarked counts as personal and is masked), and the owner is asked to approve D5 before 4a.1 fixes its content. Fix now: state that the carried values are the normalised arguments of the VERIFIED answer action, add actions (or the action.proposed payload) to carry's inputs, and have test_two_run_thread_carries_first_run_findings assert that run 2's carried item holds the shortage quantity. Also state that a GROUNDED free-text answer carries refs only, so a live run 2 may re-read but must not re-ask (core plan exit).

Global Constraints say both stores change together under conformance (ENG-STORE-1, PR-30), but 4c.3 ships the memory store only, with the Postgres tests skipped until 4c.4, while its gate set is full and pg. A pg gate whose new tests skip is not a pass for them. Also, the API-level foreign-conversation test (Review Focus 5, 'on both stores and through the API') and the 4d.5 e2e test live in tests/unit/server, which the pg gate's path set does not run. Fix: merge 4c.3 and 4c.4, or drop pg from 4c.3 and say conformance on both stores closes at 4c.4. Run the server conversation tests on Postgres through eng-verify, or state they run on memory only.

Core plan Phase 0's exit evidence has no task. It asks for a live odoo19-learning 'hi → hi → question' run with no undefined, a single reply label and the correct chip copy. The Live check section and the Self-review spec coverage cover only the Phase 1 exit. Fix: add the Phase 0 live items to 4f.2, or state they are fixture evidence only (ENG-EVID-2).

Concern (b) is real. D7 is coherent (carried items reach the model only through the pack). But it makes 4f.2 the first live write with context_assembler: on, which the Phase 3 handoff gates, and it puts two new features into one live write. If it fails or the model proposes no PO, as in both Phase 3 tries, neither the Phase 3 gap nor the Phase 4 exit can be attributed. Fix: before the thread, run a single-run draft PO with context_assembler on and conversations off. Record that the owner's 4f.2 instruction is the Phase 3 ruling. State that no PO means the exit is partial and does not block the merge, as in Phase 3.

4d.1 says another requester gets FORBIDDEN (test_other_requester_is_forbidden). Global Constraints, Review Focus 5 and 4d.4 say a foreign conversation looks absent (NOT_FOUND, PR-24), and get_conversation already filters by owner, so FORBIDDEN is unreachable. Pick NOT_FOUND and rename the test.

The scope of test_every_v1_route_has_an_authorization_dependency is unclear. Its 'exactly three' allow-list includes /health/live and /health/ready, which are not /v1. If it enumerates all app.routes, FastAPI's default /openapi.json, /docs, /docs/oauth2-redirect and /redoc (FastAPI() keeps the default docs_url) and the static Mount fail it. Choose one scope, all APIRoutes or /v1 only, and make the allow-list match (PR-27, PR-06).

ag-* stop gates in 4b. 4b.4 runs ag-ux-review and resolves its findings in the same task and commit, but ag-ux-review's stop gate makes resolution a separate task. ag-ui-implement's stop gate needs an owner review before the next design stage, and no owner gate sits between 4b and 4e.1. 4e.7 does this correctly with 4.U<n> tasks.
Type consistency gap. 4c.3 returns ConversationPage and 4d.4 returns ConversationList, and neither is in 4c.2's record list or the Self-review type list. MemberFeatures is also unlisted.
Task 4f.2 has no Files section (the handoff it writes to), and its step names no command with an expected output. plan-sections.md item 9 requires both.

Concern (c). 24 tasks and four serial owner gates (G-A, G-B, G-C, G-D) with one cut line is thin. 4e.5 (the D10 citation and explanation UI) comes from the Phase 3 handoff, not roadmap row 4, and is the natural second cut line. The second-reviewer list also omits 4c.4, whose FOR UPDATE check in the run-creating transaction is Review Focus 6's concurrency path.
The edited README status paragraph still says 'eight ERP tasks'. The domain pack ships 10 task definitions (commit e408cc3), though two of them may not count as ERP tasks; check the wording.
